title: UEFA bans Gianluca Prestianni over Vinicius Jr incident – but for homophobia, not racism
content:
Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni has been given a six-match suspension for his involvement in an incident with Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior during a Champions League game in February.

At the time, Vinicius Jr alleged Prestianni had racially abused him during the Champions League play-off first leg, leading UEFA — which organises the Champions League — to open a disciplinary investigation into potential discriminatory conduct.

Prestianni denied the allegations on social media. “I want to clarify that at no time did I direct racist insults to Vini Jr, who regrettably misunderstood what he thought he heard,” a statement read. “I was never racist with anyone and I regret the threats I received from Real Madrid players.”

On Friday, UEFA confirmed that Prestianni had been banned, but for homophobic conduct, rather than racist. Three games of Prestianni’s six-match ban are suspended for two years, while UEFA says the game the Argentine missed having been suspended “without prejudice” for the reverse fixture in Madrid later that month counts towards the total.

That means Prestianni is in effect suspended for the next two games he plays in a UEFA-organised competition. UEFA’s statement added that it has made a request to FIFA, world football’s governing body, to apply the ban globally. That would include the World Cup, with Prestianni having made his Argentina debut in November and was included in Lionel Scaloni’s squad in March. The Athletic has approached FIFA for comment.

There is a three-day window to appeal the decision but Benfica sources have told The Athletic that they do not intend to.

Regarding incidents of discrimination, UEFA’s regulations say that anyone “who insults the human dignity of a person or group of persons on whatever grounds, including skin colour, race, religion, ethnic origin, gender or sexual orientation, incurs a suspension lasting at least ten matches or a specified period of time, or any other appropriate sanction.” UEFA declined to comment when asked by The Athletic why Prestianni’s ban was not for 10 matches or more.

The incident which prompted UEFA’s ethics and disciplinary body to open the investigation occurred after Vinicius Jr scored the only goal of the game in the second half.

After speaking to Vinicius Jr, referee Francois Letexier signalled the start of FIFA’s racial abuse protocol by crossing his wrists above his head. The match was stopped for around eight minutes.

The day after the game, UEFA confirmed it would be opening an investigation into the alleged offence. Discriminatory conduct carries a minimum suspension length of 10 games if proven, according to their guidelines.

Prestianni denied the allegation after the match on his social media, saying Vinicius Jr “regrettably misunderstood what he thought he heard”.

UEFA’s ethics and disciplinary inspector requested Prestianni be suspended for the second leg, which Madrid won 2-1. Benfica unsuccessfully appealed that one-game ban.

On February 27, Benfica suspended five club members for acts of “a racist nature” during the game in Lisbon on February 17.

Benfica released a statement on the club’s website outlining its “historical and unwavering commitment to defending the values ​​of equality, respect, and inclusion” and that it “fully supports and believes in the version presented by the player Gianluca Prestianni”.

Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe said after the match that he heard Prestianni “say that Vinicius is a monkey, five times”.

Benfica head coach Jose Mourinho suggested after the game that Vinicius Jr had incited the incident, also referencing the home side’s legend Eusebio, who is Black. The reference to the forward’s celebration and the Portuguese club’s history was condemned by anti-racism charity Kick it Out who said on social media that it was “a form of gaslighting” and “sends the wrong message”, while Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany described Mourinho’s comments as “a huge mistake”.

In early March, Mourinho said that Prestianni’s Benfica career would be “over” if he was found guilty of racially abusing Vinicius Jr, adding that he “completely renounced any type of discrimination or prejudice, of ignorance or idiocy.”

“I also say that if — and, I repeat, if — my player did not respect those principles — which are my principles and those of Benfica, too, then that player’s career under Jose Mourinho and at Benfica is over,” Mourinho said.

On February 28, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) confirmed their intention to ban players from covering their mouths when speaking to an opponent.
